newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWEAN SHARES START WEEK FIRM IN ACTIVE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWEAN SHARES START WEEK FIRM IN ACTIVE TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares rose one percent in an active market on Monday as investor sentiment continued bullish on the back of a "no tax raising" national budget introduced last Thursday.
The main industrial index leapt 125.53 points -- or 1.2 percent -- to close at 11,595.51.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue bullish this week although there might be some profit-taking later on.

"People were expecting a lot of taxes to be raised and introduced in the budget but that didn't come. The only tax which was significant for the market was the 15 percent withholding tax on treasury bills and that's going to be positive for equities," one broker said.
"There's no way investors are going to put a lot of money into the money market now so people are going to find the stock market more attractive," he added.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Monday, pharmaceutical group Caps leapt 250 cents to 3,350, cement producer Porthold jumped 120 cents to 2,420, finance house Finhold rose 60 cents to 700, hotels, supermarkets and beverages conglomerate Delta gained 50 cents to 2,150.
Against the trend, timber producer Border dropped 100 cents to 1,600 and hotel and supermarket group Meikles shed 15 cents to 3,125.
Minings continued lacklustre and quiet with Wankie Colliery trading 10 cents up at 620.
The mining index put on 3.74 points to 796.61.
